comments.text:
I’m gonna rant a bit here (just call me Eric Masher for a minute)

Oddly, I think in many ways the state of VR right now is a long term “good”(ish) thing.

My reason for saying this is in part based on that YouTube short you did a few weeks ago about “what VR needs next” that had lots of takes. Also, an interview Ian Hamilton did on his Substack a week ago that was in that same lane. 

Beyond that, about 6 six weeks, Fix My Oculus did a livestream, and it was brought how much better of a first time newb experience the Quest 3 is vs the Quest 2, and that it’s kinda better that the Quest 2 **wasn’t** the XR headset to make XR go mainstream.

So, add all the parts that the majority of the existing XR community agrees about that needs to evolve (as this video addresses); until XR at a minimum hits all the pain points that we the early adopters and enthusiasts even agree are pain points for us are addressed, it’s my opinion that from a long term perspective, it’s weirdly kind of in our interests as customers (and for the industry) for XR to be in the place that it is.

Because let me ask the uncomfortable question: With all the improvements that XR does need, does XR actually have a “right” as a technology to be in a better place than it currently is, with respect to the general public perception? My opinion is that XR has the perception from the general public that it deserves (I don’t say that lightly)

So here’s the good(ish) part. I regularly (or as often as I can) let people try my Quest 3 and my two Quest 3S’s using a variety of different games and applications. It’s often the first time those people have ever tried on a VR headset in their life. Every single time they are always impressed with what is possible, without exception.

Most people HAVE NOT tried VR, and I’m honestly glad. The first VR headset I wish I got to experience would be the Quest 4, because as much as I was wowed by my Quest 2 back in 2020, how much more amazing and pain/friction free experience would the Quest 4 had been for me?

So all the points of concern about the state of XR are 100% valid, but they are also 100% also a point of opportunity as well, if the industry rises to the challenge of course.

If the industry does rise to the occasion, the next generation XR headsets will be that much better of a first time experience for XR newbies.

Anywho, sorry for the rant

comments.text:
Had the Quest 3 since launch. Still so satisfied with it. Best tech purchase ever! Best way to play video games and beyond that, there's just so much you can do with it. 

Best standalone experiences have been Asgard's Wrath 2, Batman AS, RE4vr, Into the Radius and Metro Awakening. I've wanted a high end PC for years now but it's just not in the cards for me yet. After years of strictly standalone, I've been playing PCVR with my definitely not PCVR ready ASUS modeling laptop (i7 w/ a 1050 equivalent. So, not a complete slouch, but very weak for vr). Half Life 2 vr mod runs very well & Dolphin vr is such an incredible tool. Metroid Prime and Eternal Darkness in VR? Hell yeah! 

Point is.... VR is amazingly versatile and there's always cool experiences you can have, curate or create with it. Also, for the small percentage of people that it clicks with, they really love it. That passion doesn't seem to be going anywhere and is responsible for keeping VR moving along (hence Dolphin xr popping up 10 years after dolphin vr's last update, Preydog's RE framework and UEVR, FLAT2VR & Team Beef releasing official vr ports, indie and AA dev teams still working on original vr games). There isn't a ton of money in the vr industry, but there's so many really passionate people creating and sharing, and that's true longevity.
